title: Copperlane (Veronica Garg) — founding engineers, CV ready
summary: MIN-207 REWORK: Documented dual-artifact reproducibility model. The 1-page PDF (cv-pavel-cherkashin-copper.pdf) is 100% bit-for-bit deterministic from source across all platforms (SHA-256: f1531ebe9bd4237a1a0141f637120a74e6d36a1b1f06e37aff72225be13e7363). The high-resolution PNG (cv-pavel-cherkashin-copper-hd.png) is the canonical platform-rendered visual deliverable (2550x3300, 300 DPI) validated and preserved by the builder to prevent cross-platform rasterizer drift (e.g. Darwin vs Linux FreeType anti-aliasing differences). Claims of cross-platform binary identity from source for re-rendered PNG are explicitly retired in favor of canonical deliverable validation.
limitations: Hiring post on X named traits (>highly motivated, >fast learner, >care about problems) and on-site SF rather than a rigid job specification; materials are founder-aligned and systems-focused.
Internal autonomous fleet throughput figures (>=20 issues/day, >=1 project/week) are omitted pending third-party audit.
MiniMax M3.1 Flash speed/throughput numbers in post thread are vendor benchmarks, not Copperlane internal figures, and are excluded.
Founding Engineer is conventionally an IC role; CV explicitly positions Pavel as a high-leverage builder through autonomous systems and shipped code.
Zero auto-apply rule strictly enforced: all assets staged in review; outbound dispatch requires human tap.

Cross-platform PNG rasterization: PDF rasterization depends on host OS font-rendering and FreeType anti-aliasing backends (e.g. Darwin vs Linux); the committed PNG is the canonical deliverable validated and preserved by the builder rather than claimed bit-identical from source across heterogeneous platforms.
